### The United States Department of Agriculture released market prices for **pumpkins** in 13 cities in the United States from September 24, 2016 to September 30, 2017. The `pumpkin-prices-data.csv` file, which you can access on the [GitHub](https://github.com/jhelmer3/PSYC6019-2026/blob/main/lab/data/lab_07/pumpkin_prices_data.csv) contains these prices from the Atlanta data file. 

You can read more about the data here: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/usda/a-year-of-pumpkin-prices/data (but please use the version I added to our GitHub for this assignment).

The `price` variable contains the price sold at per 1,000 pounds of pumpkins. The `variety` variable contains the type of pumpkin: `HOWDEN TYPE` is the classic Jack-O-Lantern style pumpkin, and `PIE TYPE` is the type used for pumpkin pies! Your task is to examine if there are differences in market price between Howden Type and Pie Type pumpkins in the Bayesian framework.

First, read the data in and use a few functions to explore the data. Convert `variety` to a factor, and use the factor version for the rest of the analysis.
